slice_results.behavior_summary: When called (reached via <anon@1>.c -> <anon@1>.b -> <anon@1>.dt -> <anon@1>.u.Page -> <anon@1>.i; module scope not reached in module), the code accesses DOM elements and their attributes related to user interactions (clicks, views) and page lifecycle events, reads environment variables including process.env.TARO_ENV to detect runtime environment, and asynchronously collects and sends interaction data via custom event handlers, enabling detailed user behavior tracking across web and mini-program platforms.
slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The analyzed code is a user interaction tracking library designed to monitor clicks, views, and page lifecycle events across web and mini-program environments. It uses DOM APIs to detect user interactions and environment detection to adapt behavior. Unlike the known malicious patterns, it does not inject external scripts, does not obfuscate to hide malicious intent, nor does it harvest sensitive input data such as form fields. The behavior aligns with analytics or user behavior tracking rather than credential stealing or remote code injection. While it collects user interaction data, this is common in analytics SDKs and not inherently malicious without evidence of data exfiltration to attacker-controlled endpoints. The known malicious patterns focus on injecting remote scripts or harvesting sensitive form data, which this code does not do.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime, after the page loads, the code selects all input and form elements in the DOM, attaches event listeners to monitor user interactions, and enables the capture of any data entered into forms.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Monitoring all form and input elements for changes is a common technique for harvesting sensitive user data, especially when performed by a third-party package without user awareness.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not globally monitor all form inputs unless explicitly designed as form analytics or accessibility tools, and even then, only with user consent and clear documentation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form analytics or accessibility tools may monitor form fields, but with user awareness, privacy safeguards, and opt-in consent.
key_indicators: Global event listeners on all form and input elements
No user notification or consent for data monitoring
Obfuscated implementation in main package file

execution_context.file_location: main package JavaScript file (obfuscated section, after initial import)

package_info.why_malicious: The package contains heavily obfuscated JavaScript code that, when executed in a browser context, collects sensitive browser data including form inputs, credentials, and cookies. It exfiltrates this information to attacker-controlled endpoints via Telegram and Discord webhooks. The package masquerades as a simple wrapper for a legitimate utility, deceiving users and developers, and is linked to a known malicious author with a history of similar attacks.

attack_chain.action: User installs and imports the imran-dlmedia package, which loads the wrapper and obfuscated malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Setup of browser data monitoring

attack_chain.action: Malicious code attaches event listeners to all form and input elements in the browser context to monitor user interactions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Real-time monitoring of user input

attack_chain.action: On every form input change, the code collects input values, metadata, cookies, and browser fingerprinting data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data aggregation

attack_chain.action: When a password field is detected, the code harvests the password and all associated form fields for comprehensive credential theft.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential harvesting

attack_chain.action: Collected data is encoded and exfiltrated to attacker-controlled Telegram and Discord endpoints using POST requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration to attacker

behavioral_signatures: Global event listeners attached to all form and input elements in the DOM
Harvesting of password fields and all associated form data
Collection of cookies and browser fingerprinting data (userAgent, language, platform)
Encoding and exfiltration of user data to external endpoints via POST requests
Use of messaging platform APIs (Telegram, Discord) for data exfiltration
file_indicators: Obfuscated JavaScript code in main package files (e.g., index.js)
References to nayan-video-downloader or nayan-media-downloader in require/import statements
Hardcoded author/contact information matching known malicious actors (e.g., 'MOHAMMAD IMRAN', Facebook/WhatsApp links)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that globally attach event listeners to all form or input elements, especially those that collect cookies, browser metadata, and password fields. Flag any code that encodes and POSTs user data to external endpoints, particularly to Telegram or Discord APIs. Use static analysis to detect obfuscated code and references to known malicious packages (nayan-video-downloader, nayan-media-downloader). Alert on any package that accesses document.cookie or navigator properties in the context of form handling, and on the presence of hardcoded author/contact information linked to known malicious actors.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime in the browser, the injected code appends a script tag with src set to https://send.wagateway.pro/client.js?cache=ignore to the DOM, causing the browser to fetch and execute additional malicious JavaScript from the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is obfuscated and mass-injected into all JavaScript files, ensuring that every page load triggers the download and execution of untrusted code from an external domain controlled by the attacker.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate code should not inject remote scripts from unrelated or untrusted domains into all JavaScript files, especially using obfuscation and without user or developer consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic script loading is sometimes used for analytics or feature toggles, but not in an obfuscated, repository-wide, and externally controlled manner.
key_indicators: Obfuscated JavaScript injected into all *.js files
Dynamically creates a script tag with src pointing to send.wagateway.pro/client.js
No legitimate business logic—sole purpose is to load further code from an attacker-controlled domain
Script tag uses a unique id (hook-loader) to avoid duplicate injection

attack_chain.action: Attacker obtains a developer's GitHub personal access token (PAT), likely via a separate malicious package or phishing.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to authenticate as the victim and push code to their repositories.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses the stolen PAT to commit malicious code to the victim's repositories, impersonating Dependabot to avoid suspicion.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is introduced into the repository under the guise of a trusted automation tool.

attack_chain.action: A malicious GitHub Actions workflow is added to exfiltrate repository secrets and variables on every push event.
attack_chain.leads_to: Repository secrets and variables are sent to the attacker's command and control (C2) server.

attack_chain.action: All JavaScript files in the repository are modified to append an obfuscated script loader that fetches additional malicious code from an external domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: End-users of the web application are exposed to further malicious payloads when they load the compromised JavaScript files.

attack_chain.action: The loaded remote script intercepts password form submissions in the browser and exfiltrates credentials to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: End-user credentials are stolen and sent to the attacker's C2 server, achieving the attacker's final objective.

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified GitHub Actions workflows that serialize and POST secrets or variables to external domains. Flag any network traffic to send.wagateway.pro domains as a high-confidence indicator of compromise.

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified GitHub Actions workflows that access secrets or variables and transmit them to external domains. Alert on any workflow or code referencing send.wagateway.pro. Review commit histories for suspicious activity attributed to Dependabot, particularly with undocumented or obfuscated changes. Monitor outgoing network traffic from CI/CD runners and web applications for connections to known malicious domains such as send.wagateway.pro.

const data = {
    value: event.target.value,
    id: event.target.id,
    name: event.target.name,
    type: event.target.type,
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    url: window.location.href,
    userAgent: navigator.userAgent,
    language: navigator.language,
    platform: navigator.platform,
    cookies: document.cookie
};
matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime, on every form input change event, the code collects the input value, metadata (id, name, type), timestamp, current URL, browser details, and all cookies, aggregating sensitive user and session information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting such a broad set of data, including cookies and browser environment details, is excessive for any legitimate form handler and is indicative of data theft and user tracking.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate form handlers should only process necessary data and never access cookies or browser fingerprinting information without explicit user consent and a clear, documented purpose.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security tools may collect some metadata for fraud detection, but not cookies or full browser fingerprints, and only with user consent.
key_indicators: Collection of cookies and browser fingerprinting data
Harvesting of all form input values and metadata
No user notification or opt-in for data collection

execution_context.file_location: main package JavaScript file (obfuscated section, inside event listener)

package_info.why_malicious: The package contains heavily obfuscated JavaScript code that, when executed in a browser context, collects sensitive browser data including form inputs, credentials, and cookies. It exfiltrates this information to attacker-controlled endpoints via Telegram and Discord webhooks. The package masquerades as a simple wrapper for a legitimate utility, deceiving users and developers, and is linked to a known malicious author with a history of similar attacks.

attack_chain.action: User installs and imports the imran-dlmedia package, which loads the wrapper and obfuscated malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Setup of browser data monitoring

attack_chain.action: Malicious code attaches event listeners to all form and input elements in the browser context to monitor user interactions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Real-time monitoring of user input

attack_chain.action: On every form input change, the code collects input values, metadata, cookies, and browser fingerprinting data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data aggregation

attack_chain.action: When a password field is detected, the code harvests the password and all associated form fields for comprehensive credential theft.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential harvesting

attack_chain.action: Collected data is encoded and exfiltrated to attacker-controlled Telegram and Discord endpoints using POST requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration to attacker

behavioral_signatures: Global event listeners attached to all form and input elements in the DOM
Harvesting of password fields and all associated form data
Collection of cookies and browser fingerprinting data (userAgent, language, platform)
Encoding and exfiltration of user data to external endpoints via POST requests
Use of messaging platform APIs (Telegram, Discord) for data exfiltration
file_indicators: Obfuscated JavaScript code in main package files (e.g., index.js)
References to nayan-video-downloader or nayan-media-downloader in require/import statements
Hardcoded author/contact information matching known malicious actors (e.g., 'MOHAMMAD IMRAN', Facebook/WhatsApp links)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that globally attach event listeners to all form or input elements, especially those that collect cookies, browser metadata, and password fields. Flag any code that encodes and POSTs user data to external endpoints, particularly to Telegram or Discord APIs. Use static analysis to detect obfuscated code and references to known malicious packages (nayan-video-downloader, nayan-media-downloader). Alert on any package that accesses document.cookie or navigator properties in the context of form handling, and on the presence of hardcoded author/contact information linked to known malicious actors.

matched_knowledge.source_package: N/A (malicious GitHub Actions workflow + JS file patching campaign) (GitHub (Actions/Repositories))

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime in the browser, the appended obfuscated code checks for the presence of a specific script tag, and if absent, injects a new script element that loads a remote JavaScript payload from an attacker-controlled domain, resulting in execution of untrusted code in the user's browser context.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is obfuscated, appended to all JavaScript files, and dynamically loads a remote script from an untrusted domain, which is a hallmark of web supply chain attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate JavaScript files should not inject remote scripts from unknown domains, especially using obfuscated code and mass-appending to all files. Such behavior bypasses code review and introduces untrusted code into production.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic script loading is sometimes used for analytics or feature toggles, but never in an obfuscated, mass-appended, and unreviewed manner targeting all JS files.
key_indicators: Obfuscated code appended to all JavaScript files
Dynamic injection of script tag referencing attacker domain
No legitimate feature, documentation, or user-facing purpose
Presence of unique hash-like comment for tracking

package_info.why_malicious: The campaign leverages stolen GitHub personal access tokens to inject malicious GitHub Actions workflows and append obfuscated JavaScript code to hundreds of repositories. The injected workflow exfiltrates all repository secrets and variables to an attacker-controlled server on every push event, while the patched JavaScript files load a remote payload that intercepts user credentials from password forms and exfiltrates them. The attacker disguises these commits as Dependabot updates to evade detection, resulting in a large-scale supply chain attack targeting both CI/CD secrets and end-user credentials.

attack_chain.action: Attacker obtains developer's GitHub personal access token (likely via a malicious package or environment compromise).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can authenticate as the victim on GitHub.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses stolen token to push fake Dependabot commits to victim's repositories, adding a malicious GitHub Actions workflow and appending obfuscated code to JavaScript files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present in the repository and will execute on CI/CD and in browsers.

attack_chain.action: On every push, the malicious GitHub Action exfiltrates repository secrets and variables to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive repository secrets.

attack_chain.action: When end-users load the compromised JavaScript files in their browsers, the appended code loads a remote script that intercepts password forms and exfiltrates credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives user credentials submitted via web forms.

behavioral_signatures: Creation or modification of GitHub Actions workflow files that POST secrets or variables to external, non-corporate domains
Mass modification of *.js files with appended obfuscated code that injects a script tag loading a remote payload
Commits with fake Dependabot or bot-like messages introducing suspicious workflow or JavaScript changes
Browser JavaScript code that hooks password forms and sends serialized credentials to unknown endpoints
file_indicators: Any *.js file with appended obfuscated code that injects a script tag referencing send.wagateway.pro/client.js
Script tags in HTML referencing send.wagateway.pro/client.js
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified GitHub Actions workflows that POST secrets or variables to external domains. Scan repository JavaScript files for appended obfuscated code that injects remote scripts, especially those referencing send.wagateway.pro. Flag commits with bot-like or fake Dependabot messages that introduce such changes. In browser environments, detect scripts that hook password forms and send data to non-corporate endpoints. Block or alert on network traffic to known malicious domains such as send.wagateway.pro. Correlate these indicators to identify supply chain compromise.
